hard_gates.evidence: The pale-green oval stone has a closed continuous silver rim around its perimeter, visibly separate from the interior stone. The small beaded surface of the rim does not break its encircling boundary; no gem grade or hidden safety claim is inferred.
The dark ink-blue skirt begins at a visible upper band and descends in broad continuous pleats through the lower frame.
Both visible arms continue from the same subject through sleeves to her wrists and hands. The case-gripping hand and free hand belong to that subject; the ornament sits on her upper garment.

The shoulders, elbows, wrists and fingers form coherent connected chains. A low case handle is grasped with a relaxed extended arm, and the other hand rests near the skirt without an implausible reach.

The torso is upright over the skirt with no visible unsupported lean. Feet are outside the crop and ordinary standing support is accounted for. The case hangs below its grasped handle; the norigae follows a gravity-aligned cord from the garment knot.

The case-handle grip and garment layer junction are coherent, but the governing norigae upper loop is hidden behind the goreum knot, and the separate pendant bail-to-cord bridge cannot be directly assessed. Those intended critical connections are not established at native scale.

The face, collar, goreum, skirt band and stone rim are in frame and readable. The upper attachment loop and tiny pendant bail lack separately readable boundaries at native scale, so the view does not make every critical relation assessable.
